ap_calculus_ab-f01.title: Closest point on a curved path to a fixed station: distance and its derivative, minimum distance, perpendicular condition, rate of change of distance

stimulus.description: A drone flying above a curved path, a ground station at a fixed point

data.model: path y = ln(x), x > 0; station at (3, 0); distances in kilometers

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A drone flies along the path $y=\ln x$ for $0.5\le x\le 8$, where $x$ and $y$ are in kilometers. A ground station is located at the point $(3,0)$. Let $D(x)$ be the distance, in kilometers, from the station to the drone when the drone is at the point $(x,\ln x)$. Find $D(2)$ and $D'(2)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of the distance at the given position
Value of the derivative of the distance at the given position

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the value of $x$ for which the drone is closest to the station. Find that least distance and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $D'(x)=0$ at $x=2.632$. $D'$ changes from negative to positive there, and it is the only critical point on the interval, so the least distance is $D(2.632)=1.035$ kilometers.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the derivative of the distance equal to zero and solves with a calculator
Justification: $D'$ changes sign from negative to positive at this value, so the distance has a minimum
Least distance

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At the point of the path closest to the station, show that the line segment from the station to the drone is perpendicular to the line tangent to the path.
parts.model_answer: The tangent slope is $\frac{1}{x}=0.380$ at $x=2.632$. The segment from $(3,0)$ to $(2.632,\ln 2.632)$ has slope $\frac{\ln x}{x-3}=-2.630$. The product of the slopes is -0.999, approximately $-1$, so the lines are perpendicular.

rubric_rows.criterion: Slope of the tangent line and slope of the segment at the closest point
Conclusion: the product of the slopes is negative one, so the lines are perpendicular

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The drone moves along the path so that $x$ is increasing at a constant rate of $4$ kilometers per minute. Find the rate at which the distance from the station to the drone is changing at the instant $x=2$. Using correct units, state whether the distance is increasing or decreasing.
parts.model_answer: $\frac{dD}{dt}=D'(2)\cdot\frac{dx}{dt}=-0.537\cdot 4=-2.148$ kilometers per minute, so the distance is decreasing.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the chain rule: the rate of the distance is the derivative of D times the rate of x
Value with units, and whether the distance is increasing or decreasing

ap_calculus_ab-f02.title: Cooling model: verify the differential equation, tangent-line estimate, over or under by concavity, time to a target temperature and the rate then

stimulus.description: Temperature of a cast-iron pan cooling in a kitchen

data.model: T(t) = 24 + 176e^(-0.04t) degrees Celsius, t in minutes; dT/dt = -0.04(T - 24)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cast-iron pan is taken out of an oven and left in a kitchen. Its temperature, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by $T(t)=24+176e^{-0.04t}$, where $t$ is the time in minutes since the pan was taken out. Show that $T$ satisfies the differential equation $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-0.04\,(T-24)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Differentiates the model
Rewrites the exponential term as T minus the room temperature and concludes the equation holds

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=T(t)$ at $t=10$. Use this tangent line to approximate the temperature of the pan at $t=15$.
parts.model_answer: $T(10)=141.976$ and $T'(10)=-4.719$, so the tangent line is $y=141.976+(-4.719)(t-10)$. At $t=15$ the approximation is $118.381$ degrees Celsius.

rubric_rows.criterion: Tangent line equation using the value and the slope at the given time
Approximation at the later time

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Is the approximation in part (b) less than or greater than the actual temperature $T(15)$? Use $\dfrac{d^2T}{dt^2}$ to justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $T''(t)=0.2816e^{-0.04t}>0$, so the graph of $T$ is concave up and lies above its tangent lines. The approximation $118.381$ is less than the actual value $T(15)=120.591$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justification: the second derivative of the model is positive, so the function is concave up
Conclusion: the tangent line is below a concave up graph, so the approximation is less than the actual temperature

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The pan can be handled safely once its temperature reaches $100$ degrees Celsius. Find the time $t$ at which $T(t)=100$. Using correct units, find the rate of change of the temperature at that time.
parts.model_answer: $T(t)=100$ gives $t=20.994$ minutes. At that time $T'(t)=-0.04(100-24)=-3.040$ degrees Celsius per minute.

rubric_rows.criterion: Equation for the time
Time (calculator)
Rate of change at that time with units: degrees Celsius per minute (negative: the pan is cooling)

ap_calculus_ab-f03.title: Region between a sine curve and a line: intersection, area, vertical line bisecting the area, greatest vertical distance

stimulus.description: A region between a sine curve and a line

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $R$ be the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the curve $y=6\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$ and the line $y=0.8x$. Find the $x$-coordinate of the point, other than the origin, where the curve and the line intersect.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the two expressions equal to find the intersection
Solution with a calculator

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the area of $R$. Show the setup for your calculation.

rubric_rows.criterion: Integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve between the limits found in part (a)
Value of the area

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The vertical line $x=k$, with $0<k<$ the $x$-coordinate found in part (a), divides $R$ into two regions of equal area. Write an equation involving an integral that gives $k$, and find the value of $k$.
parts.model_answer: The area of the left piece must be half of the total: $\int_0^{k}\left(6\sin(x/3)-0.8x\right)dx=5.608$, which gives $k=3.348$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses half of the total area from part (b) as the target
Equation with an integral from zero to k of the difference of the curves equal to half of the area
Value of k

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For $0\le x\le$ the $x$-coordinate found in part (a), find the greatest vertical distance between the curve and the line. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The vertical distance is $g(x)=6\sin(x/3)-0.8x$, and $g'(x)=2\cos(x/3)-0.8=0$ at $x=3.478$. $g'$ changes from positive to negative there and $g=0$ at both ends, so the greatest distance is $g(3.478)=2.717$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the derivative of the vertical distance equal to zero and solves
Justification: $g'$ changes from positive to negative (or the endpoint values are zero), and the greatest distance value
required_elements: $g'$ changes sign from positive to negative

ap_calculus_ab-f04.title: A function with an inverse tangent term: derivative, relative maximum, a limit at infinity, number of zeros

stimulus.description: A function containing an inverse tangent term

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $f$ be the function defined by $f(x)=2\arctan x-x$ for all real $x$. Find $f'(x)$ and find all values of $x$ for which $f'(x)=0$.
parts.model_answer: $f'(x)=\frac{2}{1+x^2}-1=\frac{\left(1-x^2\right)}{1+x^2}$, which is $0$ when $x^2=1$, that is, $x=\pm1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Derivative using the derivative of the inverse tangent
Solves $f'(x)=0$ for both values

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that $f$ has a relative maximum at $x=1$, and find the value of this relative maximum. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $f'(x)$ is positive for $-1<x<1$ and negative for $x>1$, so $f'$ changes from positive to negative at $x=1$ and $f$ has a relative maximum there. $f(1)=2\arctan(1)-1\cdot 1=-1 + \frac{\pi}{2}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justification: $f'$ changes sign from positive to negative at $x=1$ (sign analysis on both sides)
required_elements: $f'$ changes from positive to negative at $x=1$

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of the relative maximum, using the exact value of the inverse tangent

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{f(x)}{x}$. Show the work that leads to your answer.
parts.model_answer: $\frac{f(x)}{x}=2\cdot\frac{\arctan x}{x}-1$. Since $-\frac{\pi}{2}<\arctan x<\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\frac{\arctan x}{x}\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$, so the limit is $-1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Rewrites the quotient as the inverse tangent term over $x$ minus a constant
Reason that $\frac{\arctan x}{x}\to 0$: the inverse tangent is bounded (or approaches $\frac{\pi}{2}$) while $x\to\infty$
Value of the limit

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: How many solutions does the equation $f(x)=0$ have? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $f(0)=0$. On $\left[0,1\right]$, $f$ is increasing from $0$ to $f(1)=-1 + \frac{\pi}{2}>0$, and on $\left[1,\infty\right)$, $f$ is decreasing and continuous with $f(x)\to-\infty$, because $f(x)\le 2\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}-x$. By the Intermediate Value Theorem and monotonicity, there is exactly one solution with $x>1$. Since $f$ is odd, there is exactly one solution with $x<-1$. So $f(x)=0$ has $3$ solutions.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the behavior of $f$ on each interval using the sign of $f'$, including the positive value $f(1)$ and $f(0)=0$
Justification by the Intermediate Value Theorem on each side, and the total of three solutions

ap_calculus_ab-f05.title: Exponential decay differential equation: separation of variables, half-life, time to a given mass, average mass

stimulus.description: Radioactive tracer in a sealed capsule

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A sealed capsule holds $18$ grams of a radioactive tracer. Let $M(t)$ be the mass of the tracer, in grams, remaining $t$ years after the capsule is sealed. The rate at which the mass decreases is proportional to the mass present, so $\frac{dM}{dt}=-kM$ for a positive constant $k$. Use separation of variables to find an expression for $M(t)$ in terms of $k$.
parts.model_answer: $\frac{1}{M}\,dM=-k\,dt$; $\ln|M|=-kt+C$; $M=Ce^{-kt}$ and $M(0)=18$ gives $M(t)=18e^{-kt}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Separates the variables
Antiderivatives of both sides with a constant of integration
Solves for $M$ and uses the initial mass to find the constant

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The half-life of the tracer is $4$ years, that is, $M(4)=\frac12 M(0)$. Find $k$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of $k$ from the half-life condition

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At what time $t$ will $6$ grams of the tracer remain? Express your answer in terms of natural logarithms.
parts.model_answer: $18e^{-kt}=6$ gives $e^{-kt}=\frac{1}{3}$, so $t=\frac{\ln 3}{k}=\frac{4\ln 3}{\ln 2}$ years.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up and solves the exponential equation by taking logarithms
Value of $t$ with the value of $k$ substituted

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the average mass of the tracer in the capsule over the time interval $0\le t\le 8$ years. Give your answer in grams, in exact form.
parts.model_answer: $\frac{1}{8}\int_0^{8}18e^{-kt}\,dt=\frac{18}{8k}\left(1-e^{-8k}\right)=\frac{18}{8k}\left(1-\frac14\right)=\frac{27}{4 \ln 2}$ grams.

rubric_rows.criterion: Integral setup for the average value, with division by the length of the interval
Antiderivative and evaluation using $e^{-8k}=\frac14$
Exact value of the average mass with units

ap_calculus_ab-f06.title: An accumulation function with upper limit x squared: derivative, tangent line, relative extrema, limit at zero

stimulus.description: A function defined by an integral with a variable upper limit

data.definition: H(x) = integral from 0 to x^2 of (e^t - 2) dt

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $H$ be the function defined by $H(x)=\int_0^{x^2}\left(e^t-2\right)dt$. Find $H'(x)$.
parts.model_answer: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and the chain rule, $H'(x)=\left(e^{x^2}-2\right)\cdot 2x$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: the integrand evaluated at the upper limit
Chain rule factor from the upper limit; the final expression for the derivative

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=H(x)$ at $x=1$.
parts.model_answer: $H(1)=\int_0^1\left(e^t-2\right)dt=-3 + e$ and $H'(1)=2(e-2)=-4 + 2 e$, so the tangent line is $y=\left(-4 + 2 e\right)(x-1)+\left(-3 + e\right)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of $H(1)$ by evaluating the integral and the slope $H'(1)$
Equation of the tangent line

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the $x$-coordinate of each relative extremum of $H$ and classify each as a relative maximum or a relative minimum. Justify your answers.
parts.model_answer: $H'(x)=2x\left(e^{x^2}-2\right)=0$ at $x=0$ and $x=\pm\sqrt{\ln 2}$. $H'<0$ for $x<-\sqrt{\ln 2}$, $H'>0$ on $\left(-\sqrt{\ln 2},0\right)$, $H'<0$ on $\left(0,\sqrt{\ln 2}\right)$, and $H'>0$ for $x>\sqrt{\ln 2}$. So $H$ has a relative maximum at $x=0$ and relative minima at $x=\pm\sqrt{\ln 2}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Critical points from setting $H'(x)=0$
Justification: signs of $H'$ on the intervals determined by the critical points (sign changes of $H'$)
Classification of all three critical points as the reason requires: a relative maximum at the middle one and relative minima at the other two

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{H(x)}{x^2}$. Show the work that leads to your answer, including why the method you use applies.
parts.model_answer: $H(0)=0$ and $x^2\to 0$, so the form is $\frac00$ and L’Hospital’s Rule applies: $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{H'(x)}{2x}=\lim_{x\to 0}\left(e^{x^2}-2\right)=1-2=-1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the indeterminate form $\frac00$ (both numerator and denominator approach $0$) before differentiating
Applies L’Hospital’s Rule with $H'(x)$ from part (a) and gives the value

So $H$ has a relative maximum at $x=0$ and relative minima at $x=\pm\sqrt{\ln 2}$.

ap_calculus_ab-f07.title: Limits with L’Hospital’s Rule: a removable value, a repeated application, and a limit at infinity with a horizontal asymptote

stimulus.description: Three limit problems and a continuity condition

data.functions: The functions g and h are defined in parts (b) and (d).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{x^2-1}{\ln x}$. Show the work that leads to your answer, including why the method you use applies.
parts.model_answer: Substituting $x=1$ gives $\frac{0}{0}$, so L’Hospital’s Rule applies: $\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{2x^{1}}{1/x}=\lim_{x\to 1}2x^{2}=2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the indeterminate form $\frac00$ (numerator and denominator both approach $0$)
Differentiates numerator and denominator
Value of the limit

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let $g$ be the function defined by $g(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{\ln x}$ for $x>0$ with $x\ne 1$, and $g(1)=c$. For what value of $c$ is $g$ continuous at $x=1$? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $g$ is continuous at $x=1$ exactly when $\lim_{x\to 1}g(x)=g(1)$, so $c=2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of $c$ with the condition that the limit equals the function value
required_elements: the limit equals the function value

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^x-1-x}{x^2}$. Show the work that leads to your answer.
parts.model_answer: The form is $\frac{0}{0}$; L’Hospital’s Rule gives $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^x-1}{2x}$, again $\frac{0}{0}$; applying it once more gives $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^x}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the form $\frac00$ and applies L’Hospital’s Rule once
Recognizes that the new form is still $\frac00$ and applies the rule again
Value of the limit

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Let $h(x)=\frac{6x^2+5\ln x}{3x^2}$ for $x>0$. Find $\lim_{x\to\infty}h(x)$ and write an equation for the horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=h(x)$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $h(x)=\frac{6}{3}+\frac{5}{3}\cdot\frac{\ln x}{x^2}$. The form $\frac{\ln x}{x^2}$ is $\frac{\infty}{\infty}$ and L’Hospital’s Rule gives $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{1/x}{2x}=0$. So $\lim_{x\to\infty}h(x)=2$ and the horizontal asymptote is $y=2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Shows $\frac{\ln x}{x^2}\to 0$ with a valid reason such as the $\frac{\infty}{\infty}$ form and the derivative ratio

ap_calculus_ab-f08.title: A rational function with unknown constants: critical-point conditions, limits at infinity, global extrema, number of solutions

stimulus.description: A rational function with unknown constants

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $f$ be the function given by $f(x)=\frac{Ax}{x^2+B}$, where $A$ and $B$ are positive constants. The function $f$ has a critical point at $x=1$, and $f(1)=1$. Find $A$ and $B$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Derivative of $f$ by the quotient rule
Uses $f'(p)=0$ to find $B$
Uses the value of $f$ to find $A$; both constants stated

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For the values of $A$ and $B$ found in part (a), find $\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)$, and give an equation for the horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=f(x)$.
parts.model_answer: Both limits equal $0$; the horizontal asymptote is $y=0$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of both limits and the equation of the horizontal asymptote

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Show that $f$ has an absolute maximum value of $1$ and an absolute minimum value of $-1$ on the interval $-\infty<x<\infty$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $f'(x)=\frac{2(1-x^2)}{(x^2+1)^2}$ is negative for $x<-1$, positive for $-1<x<1$, and negative for $x>1$. So $f$ has a relative minimum at $x=-1$ with $f(-1)=-1$ and a relative maximum at $x=1$ with $f(1)=1$. Since $f(x)\to 0$ as $x\to\pm\infty$ and $-1<0<1$, no value outside $[-1,1]$ occurs, so these are the absolute extreme values.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sign of $f'$ on the three intervals determined by the critical points
Classifies the critical points and gives the values of $f$ there
Reason that no other value is larger or smaller: the limits at infinity are $0$ and there are no other critical points
required_elements: there are no other critical points, so these extreme values are absolute

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For which values of the constant $k$ does the equation $f(x)=k$ have exactly two solutions? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: On $(-\infty,-1]$, $f$ decreases from values near $0$ to $-1$; on $[-1,1]$, $f$ increases from $-1$ to $1$ and equals $0$ only at $x=0$; on $[1,\infty)$, $f$ decreases from $1$ toward $0$ without reaching it. By the Intermediate Value Theorem and monotonicity on each piece, each $k$ with $0<k<1$ is attained once on $(0,1)$ and once on $(1,\infty)$, and each $k$ with $-1<k<0$ is attained once on $(-\infty,-1)$ and once on $(-1,0)$. The values $k=0$ and $k=\pm 1$ give exactly one solution, and $|k|>1$ gives none. So the answer is $0<|k|<1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the behavior of $f$ on each of the intervals, including the values at the extremes
Conclusion with the Intermediate Value Theorem reason: exactly two solutions when $0<|k|<1$
